- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–2% of forecast range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model overestimates; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion stabilizes.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early days (1–5) after sentiment shifts; apply +0.5–1.0% bias to first 5 forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model fails to capture momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average (e.g., 3-day sentiment avg) to adjust forecast slope.
